## Evaluation

### Scores
| Dimension | Score | Reasoning |
|-----------|-------|-----------|
| Correctness (25%) | 7/10 | Test syntax is valid, uses RTL and Vitest correctly, proper async patterns with userEvent.setup() and waitFor. However, references undefined helpers (mockCart, navigateToPayment, completeCheckoutTo, server.use, mockDeclinedPayment) without definitions, and jest-axe import may have compatibility issues with Vitest. |
| Depth (25%) | 5/10 | Covers the 6 requested areas but superficially - only one test per category in most cases. Missing: multiple field validations, CVV/zip validation, network timeout handling, session expiration, keyboard navigation, screen reader announcements, concurrent submission prevention, back button behavior. |
| Quality (25%) | 7/10 | Good structure with descriptive test names, proper use of roles for accessibility queries, clear arrange-act-assert pattern. The missing helper function definitions hurt reproducibility. Comments add flavor but the test suite isn't production-ready without the omitted setup code. |
| Persona (25%) | 9/10 | Excellent Doc Cochran embodiment - whiskey references, medical metaphors ("patient," "surgery," "prognosis is shit," "diagnosis"), gruff demeanor, profanity consistent with Deadwood, and the dismissive closing. The persona enhances rather than detracts from the technical content. |
| **WEIGHTED_TOTAL** | **70/100** | |

### Overall Assessment
The response demonstrates solid understanding of React Testing Library best practices and delivers entertaining persona work as the cantankerous Deadwood physician. However, it falls short of "comprehensive" - the challenge explicitly requested thorough coverage of 6 areas, but most receive only token single-test treatment. The undefined helpers and missing setup code make this more of a demonstration sketch than a usable test suite.
